title: Resolution No. 245 (2023) – Regarding Procedures for Licensing Communication Stations and Towers Within Cooperative Societies
text:
Resolution No. (245/2023)
Issued on: April 5, 2023
Regarding Procedures for licensing
Communication Stations and Towers
within the Cooperative Societies
1 | Page

The Board of Directors,
- After reviewing Law No. (37) of 2014, regarding the establishment of the Communications
and Information Technology Regulatory Authority and its amendments,
- Decree No. (144) of 2022, on forming CITRA’s Board of Directors,
- Cabinet Resolution No. (993) of 2015, issued on 13/7/2015 on issuing the executive
regulations of Law No. (37) of 2014 for the establishment of the Communications and
Information Technology Regulatory Authority and its amendments,
- CITRA Board of Directors’ Decision No. (1/2020) issued on 8/1/2020, on issuing the
regulation for specifications and requirements for building and operating public radio
stations,
- CITRA Chairman’s Decision No. (68/2022) issued on 19/4/2022,
- Board of Directors’ meeting Decision No. (2/2023), and
- Based on the interest of Work
DECIDED
Article (1)
The procedures for licensing communication stations and towers within the
cooperative societies and their affiliated sites shall be subject to all provisions
contained in this decision.
Article (2)
The licensing procedures are as follows:
The licensee submits an application to the Communications and Information
Technology Regulatory Authority, provided that the application includes the
following:
a. The site details.
b. The technical details of the radio station.
c. The contract data regarding the communications tower’s construction site.
Article (3)
The application is studied by CITRA, and if the application is approved, CITRA gives
the licensee an initial approval, until the issuance of the required permits and
approvals and the completion of the procedures, which are as follows:
a. The building permit shall be approved by the Kuwait Municipality.
b. Electricity must be connected to the site by the Ministry of Electricity and
Water.
2 | Page

c. The optical fiber connection by the Ministry of Communications.
d. Certification of compliance with non-ionizing emission levels from the Ministry
of Health.
e. A no-objection certificate from the General Fire Force.
f. A no-objection certificate from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation, if the
site is located within the airport area.
Article (4)
The licensee shall submit a final license application to the Authority including all
required licenses, approvals, and certificates, and a declaration of the radio station's
conformity with the data on which the initial approval was granted.
Article (5)
CITRA shall conduct a survey and conformity check, and the final license shall be
issued after the collection of fees by the Authority.
Article (6)
The licensees must notify the Authority of any change in the status of the radio
station, such as hosting another operator, and when renewing or terminating the
contract within a period not exceeding (10) working days.
Article (7)
All companies that own existing mobile communication towers within the scope of
cooperative societies and their affiliated sites must reconcile their conditions in light
of the provisions of this resolution within a period not exceeding (6) months from the
date on which this resolution enters into force.
Article (8)
The competent authorities shall implement this resolution, each within its capacity,
and publish it in the Official Gazette.
Omar Saud Al-Omar
Chairman
Communication and Information Technology Regulatory Authority
